site.name: Within Reach
site.tagline: One person. One answer. Who qualifies, what to bring, and where to go.
site.demo_notice: Every listing on this site is a sample used to show the page design. The names, numbers and addresses are placeholders and are not real services.

categories.name: Housing
categories.short: Rent, deposits, and a place to sleep
categories.lede: Help with rent you owe, a deposit you cannot cover, or somewhere to stay tonight.

urgent.label: Nowhere to sleep tonight?
urgent.body: Call first. Beds are assigned by phone and the list changes through the day.

listings.name: Emergency rent and deposit help
listings.summary: A one-time payment made straight to your landlord. It does not come to you.
qualify: You live in Missoula County.
Your household earns $2,430 a month or less for two people. Add $510 for each extra person.
You have a notice, a late fee, or a deposit you cannot pay.
You have not used this fund in the last 12 months.
bring: Photo ID for the person signing the lease
Your lease, or a letter from your landlord
The notice or bill you need help with
Last 30 days of pay stubs, or a benefits letter
Your landlord's name, phone number and mailing address
apply: Call to book a 30 minute appointment. Walk-ins are not taken.
Bring the papers above to the appointment.
A caseworker checks your papers while you wait.
You are told yes or no the same day.
If yes, payment reaches your landlord in 5 to 10 working days. Ask for a copy of the letter they send.

where.hours: Monday to Thursday, 9am to 4pm. Closed Friday.
where.bus: On the [route] bus line. Ask the driver for the [stop] stop.

listings.name: If you have an eviction notice
listings.summary: Free advice from someone who does this every day. Call the day you get the notice, not the week it expires.
qualify: Anyone renting in Missoula County.
There is no income limit for advice.
There is an income limit if you need someone to appear in court with you. Ask on the call.
bring: The notice, including the envelope it came in
Your lease
Any texts or letters between you and your landlord
apply: Call the advice line. You do not need an appointment.
Say the date on your notice first. It decides how fast things move.
You get advice on the same call.
If your case needs someone in court, they book that with you before you hang up.

listings.name: Beds for tonight
listings.summary: Shelter beds are given out by phone from 3pm. Arriving in person does not move you up the list.
qualify: Anyone 18 or over.
Under 18 is handled by a different service. The phone line will transfer you.
Couples and pets can be taken, but say so on the call.
bring: Nothing is required to get a bed.
Bring ID if you have it. It is not needed.
One bag per person fits in the lockers.
apply: Call from 3pm. Earlier calls are not held.
You are given a bed number or a place on the list.
Arrive before 8pm or the bed is released.
Check-in reopens at 3pm the next day. A bed one night does not hold it the next.

categories.name: Food
categories.short: Groceries, meals, and food for children
categories.lede: Food you can collect this week, and the monthly benefit that costs nothing to apply for.

urgent.label: No food in the house today?
urgent.body: The pantry below gives out an emergency box with no paperwork. Go in, say it is an emergency box.

listings.name: Grocery pantry
listings.summary: A week of groceries you choose yourself, once a week. No appointment.
qualify: You live in Missoula County.
There is no income check and no paperwork for the first visit.
After the first visit you give a household size and a zip code. Nothing else.
bring: Bags or a box. The pantry runs out of both.
Nothing else is required.
apply: Walk in during opening hours.
Give your household size at the desk.
You walk the aisles and choose. Staff tell you how many of each item.
Come back any time after seven days.

where.hours: Monday to Saturday, 10am to 6pm. Last entry 5:30pm.

listings.name: SNAP food benefits
listings.summary: A card topped up monthly, used like a bank card at most grocery shops. Applying is free and does not affect immigration status for most people.
qualify: Household of one earning $1,632 a month or less before tax.
Household of two earning $2,215 or less. Add $584 for each extra person.
Savings are not counted for most households.
If you are over these numbers but pay high rent or medical costs, apply anyway. Those costs are taken off.
bring: Photo ID
Social Security numbers for everyone applying
Last 30 days of pay stubs for everyone who works
Your rent or mortgage amount, and your heating bill
Childcare costs, if you pay any
apply: Apply online, by phone, or in person. All three take the same time.
An interview follows within 7 days. It is usually by phone and takes about 20 minutes.
Send any papers they ask for within 10 days or the application closes.
A decision comes within 30 days. If you have almost no income it can be 7 days, so say that on the interview.

listings.name: Free meals for children
listings.summary: A hot meal for anyone 18 or under. No sign-up, no names taken.
qualify: Anyone aged 18 or under.
No income check. No registration.
An adult may come with the child but the meal is for the child.
bring: Nothing.
apply: Turn up during serving hours.
The child eats on site. Meals cannot be taken away.

where.hours: Term time: 3:30pm to 5pm, Monday to Friday. Holidays: 11:30am to 1pm.

categories.name: Utilities
categories.lede: Help with a bill you cannot pay, and the rule that stops your heat being cut off in winter.

urgent.label: Shut-off notice in hand?
urgent.body: Call the company on the notice before you call anyone else, and say the word 'arrangement'. That pauses the shut-off while you sort out help.

listings.name: Help with heating bills
listings.summary: A payment made straight to your energy company, once per winter. Applications open 1 October.
qualify: Household of one earning $2,510 a month or less.
Household of two earning $3,282 or less. Add $772 for each extra person.
You pay for heat, whether the bill is in your name or included in your rent.
You can apply whether or not you have a shut-off notice.
bring: Photo ID
Social Security numbers for everyone in the household
Last 30 days of income for everyone who works
Your most recent heating bill, or a letter from your landlord if heat is in your rent
Your account number with the energy company
apply: Apply online or in person. Applications open 1 October and close 30 April.
A decision takes about 4 weeks.
If you have a shut-off notice, say so on the application. It moves to about 48 hours.
The payment goes to the energy company, not to you. Your next bill shows it as a credit.

listings.name: Emergency help with a shut-off
listings.summary: A smaller payment that is decided fast, for a bill already past due.
qualify: You have a shut-off notice, or your service is already off.
Household income at or below the numbers listed for heating help above.
One payment per household per year.
bring: The shut-off notice
Photo ID
Proof of income for the last 30 days
apply: Call the same day you get the notice.
They call the energy company with you on the line.
A decision is usually given within 48 hours.
You may be asked to pay part of the bill. Ask what that amount is before you agree.

listings.name: Cheaper phone and internet
listings.summary: A monthly discount on one phone or internet bill per household.
qualify: You already get SNAP, Medicaid, or another listed benefit, or
Household of one earning $2,006 a month or less. Add $707 for each extra person.
One discount per household, not per person.
bring: Photo ID
Your benefit award letter, if you have one
Proof of income for the last 30 days, if you do not
apply: Apply online, or ask at the desk for help doing it.
Approval usually takes a few days.
Take your approval to the phone or internet company. They apply the discount.
The discount does not start until you do that last step. It is the step most often missed.

categories.name: Health care
categories.short: Clinics, prescriptions, teeth, and someone to talk to
categories.lede: Care you can get without insurance, and what it costs before you walk in.

urgent.label: In crisis, or worried about someone?
urgent.body: Call or text 988 any time. It is free, and it is answered by a person.

listings.name: Clinic with no insurance needed
listings.summary: A regular doctor's appointment. The cost is set by what you earn and is agreed before you are seen.
qualify: Anyone. No insurance needed and no residency check.
The fee is set on a sliding scale. The lowest band is $25 a visit.
Nobody is turned away for being unable to pay that day. Say so at the desk.
bring: Photo ID if you have one. It is not required.
Proof of income for the last 30 days, to set your fee
A list of medicines you take, including the doses
Your insurance card, if you have one
apply: Call for an appointment. Same-week slots are usually free.
Arrive 15 minutes early the first time to set your fee.
You are told the cost before you see the doctor, not after.
Prescriptions are sent to the pharmacy of your choice.

where.hours: Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm. Saturday 9am to 1pm.

listings.name: Help paying for prescriptions
listings.summary: Covers the cost of a medicine you have been prescribed but cannot afford this month.
qualify: You have a current prescription from any doctor.
Household of one earning $2,510 a month or less. Add $772 for each extra person.
Covers most regular medicines. Does not cover over-the-counter items.
bring: The prescription, or the empty bottle with the label
Photo ID
Proof of income for the last 30 days
apply: Bring the papers to the desk. No appointment.
A decision is given while you wait, usually within 30 minutes.
If yes, they call the pharmacy and pay directly.
Collect the medicine the same day.

listings.name: Dental care
listings.summary: Fillings, extractions, and cleaning at a set low cost. Pain is seen sooner than routine work.
qualify: Anyone. No insurance needed.
Fees are fixed and listed at the desk. An extraction is $75. A cleaning is $40.
A payment plan can be set up before treatment, not after.
bring: Photo ID if you have one
A list of medicines you take
Proof of income, if you want the lower fee band
apply: Call to join the list. The wait for routine work is about 6 weeks.
If you are in pain, say so. Pain is usually seen within 3 days.
You are told the price before treatment starts.
Pay on the day, or set up a plan at the desk.

categories.name: Transportation
categories.short: Bus fare, rides, and car repairs
categories.lede: Getting to the appointment, the interview, or the pharmacy when the trip itself is the problem.

urgent.label: Need to get somewhere today?
urgent.body: The bus pass desk below hands out single-day passes on the spot, no paperwork. Ask for a day pass.

listings.name: Free and reduced bus passes
listings.summary: A monthly pass, or single-day passes while you wait for the monthly one.
qualify: You live in Missoula County.
Household of one earning $2,006 a month or less. Add $707 for each extra person.
Students, people over 62, and people with a disability qualify at any income.
Day passes are given out with no income check at all.
bring: Photo ID
Proof of address, such as a bill or a letter
Proof of income for the last 30 days, for the monthly pass only
apply: Walk in during opening hours. No appointment.
Day passes are handed over the same visit.
The monthly pass takes about a week. Ask for day passes to cover the gap.
Renew the monthly pass in the last week of each month or it lapses.

listings.name: Rides to medical appointments
listings.summary: A booked ride to and from a medical appointment, for people who cannot use the bus.
qualify: The trip has to be to a medical appointment. Other trips are not covered.
You cannot drive yourself and cannot use the bus for the trip.
No income limit, but you must book in advance.
bring: Nothing for the ride itself.
Have your appointment date, time and the clinic address ready when you call.
apply: Call at least 3 working days before the appointment. Sooner is better.
Give the appointment date, time, and address.
You are told your pickup time on the call. Write it down.
Call the same number if the appointment moves, or the ride is lost.

listings.name: Help with car repairs
listings.summary: A one-time payment toward a repair that is stopping you getting to work.
qualify: You own the car and it is registered to you.
The repair has to be what is stopping you working or getting to medical care.
Household of one earning $2,510 a month or less. Add $772 for each extra person.
One payment per household every two years.
bring: Photo ID
The vehicle registration in your name
A written estimate from a garage
Proof of income for the last 30 days
Proof you are working, or a letter from your employer
apply: Get a written estimate first. Applications without one are not reviewed.
Call to book an appointment and bring the papers above.
A decision takes about 2 weeks.
If yes, payment goes straight to the garage. Do not pay for the repair first and ask to be paid back.

about.lede: Within Reach is a plain-language directory of local assistance for people living in Missoula County. It answers the same four questions about every kind of help: who qualifies, what to bring, how to apply, and where to go.

p: Anyone in Missoula County who needs help with housing, food, utilities, healthcare or transportation. The site assumes no prior knowledge of how assistance programs work and no familiarity with the agencies that run them.
Most people looking for help are not browsing. They have one problem and a short window to solve it, often on a phone, sometimes on a weak signal. That is the person every page here is built for.

Five categories, no account, no tracking, and no search box to guess at. Every listing answers the four questions in the same order, so learning the pattern once makes every other listing take about ten seconds.
Pages are kept deliberately light. The heaviest page on this site is smaller than a single uncompressed photograph, because a directory that will not load on two bars of signal is not a directory.
A directory is only as good as its last update. A wrong phone number costs someone a trip across town they could not afford, which is worse than no listing at all.

Every listing carries a date, and that date is meant as a commitment rather than a decoration: it records when a person last confirmed the details with the agency. Who does that confirming, and how often, is the open question this project has not yet closed with the client.

The pictures here are of real places in Missoula: the Clark Fork riverfront, Main Hall below Mount Sentinel, the depot, and Fort Missoula. They are here because the brief asked for dignified images of the actual town rather than stock photography that presents hardship as something to pity.
None of them is a photograph of a service location, and none should be read as one.

places.label: University District
places.title: Main Hall and Mount Sentinel
places.text: The M on the hillside is the easiest landmark in town to navigate by, and usually the first one people learn.

places.label: Northside
places.title: The old railroad depot
places.text: The brick depot north of the river, with the bronze bear standing out front where people arrange to meet.

places.label: Fort Missoula
places.title: A logging locomotive at Fort Missoula
places.text: Fort Missoula keeps the equipment that moved the timber this valley was largely built on.

contact.intro: These contact details are placeholders for the demonstration. Nothing below reaches a real office.
contact.real: The one number on this site that is real is 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. It works 24 hours a day, by call or text, anywhere in the US.
